title: Implementing and monitoring the plan
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:33Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The closest bank point, monitoring performance, covers comparing results with a general business plan in Year 11, while the new point is about putting a marketing plan into action and revising marketing strategies at Year 12 depth, so it needs its own point.

draft.title: Implementing and monitoring the plan
card: Implementing means putting the marketing plan into action. The business carries out its strategies, such as running ads, setting prices and training staff, and gives people the budget and time to do it.
Monitoring means tracking results while the plan runs. The business compares actual results, such as sales or market share, with the marketing objectives.
If results fall short of the objectives, the business finds out why. It may then change the strategy that is not working, such as the promotion or the price.
Monitoring is ongoing, not a one-off check. Because results are measured against the objectives, the objectives must be measurable.
draft.remember: Act on the plan, track results against the objectives, and change what is not working.

a.q: Which action is an example of monitoring a marketing plan?
opts: Comparing monthly sales with the sales objective
Booking radio advertising for the new campaign
Training staff to explain the new product range
Setting the price for a product before its launch
a.why: Monitoring means checking actual results against the objectives, and comparing sales with the sales objective does this. Booking advertising is tempting, but it carries out a strategy, so it is implementing.
a.clue: Which action measures results rather than carrying out a strategy?

b.q: Tara's bakery in Orange aimed to lift online orders by 10% in six months. After three months, online orders had risen only 2%. Which response best fits the marketing process?
opts: Find out why and change the online promotion
Wait until the six months end before checking
Drop the objective because it looks too hard
Keep the strategy unchanged since it was planned
b.why: Monitoring found a shortfall against the objective, so the bakery should find the cause and change the strategy that is not working. Waiting until the end is tempting, but monitoring is ongoing and a late check delays any fix.
b.clue: Results are behind the objective, and checking happens during the plan.

a.best: Comparing monthly sales with the sales objective

b.best: Find out why and change the online promotion
